s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive subcutaneous node in the axilla with skin infiltration and episodic pain
salient_findings: Slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin
Erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm in an 'Indian file pattern'
key_facts: Woman in her 60s
Subcutaneous node in the right axilla first noticed 10 years ago
Progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
Swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
Mild episodic pain in the right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern'
Tumor cells have basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells

shortlist.label: Hidradenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches histopathology and immunohistochemistry findings, including positive staining for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, and GATA3

shortlist.label: Apocrine carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the presence of apocrine glands and positive staining for GATA3 and estrogen receptor

shortlist.label: Secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares similarities with the case's histopathological features, including the 'Indian file pattern' and positive staining for cytokeratin and GATA3

shortlist.label: Mammary analog secretory carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to secretory carcinoma, with overlapping histopathological features and positive staining for GATA3 and estrogen receptor

shortlist.label: Carcinoma en cuirasse
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of a slowly growing subcutaneous node with skin infiltration, although less common than other options

raw.rationale: The presence of a dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement, tumor cells dispersed in an 'Indian file pattern', and positivity for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies are consistent with hidradenocarcinoma, a rare malignant tumor originating from apocrine glands.

rejected.label: Apocrine carcinoma
rejected.why: While apocrine features are present, the clinical and histological findings more specifically align with hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Secretory carcinoma
rejected.why: This diagnosis is less likely due to the specific immunohistochemical profile and clinical presentation that more closely matches hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Mammary analog secretory carcinoma
rejected.why: The location and specific histological features do not align with mammary analog secretory carcinoma, which typically presents in the salivary glands or breast tissue.

rejected.label: Carcinoma en cuirasse
rejected.why: This is a clinical presentation rather than a specific tumor type and does not account for the detailed histopathological and immunohistochemical findings.
